To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
participants in our qualitative study of long-term substance use disorder recovery reported a range of factors that influenced their decision making to quit substance use and remain in recovery.

people who quit substance use after a prolonged period of substance use report having experienced significant events that motivated them to stop using, having been able to imagine a life without substance use, and having been concerned by the consequences of their substance use.

the participants recalled harmful consequences and important events during their years as substance users; pressure and concern from close friends and family members were important factors in their initial efforts toward abstinence; being able to imagine a new life and the awareness of treatment options promoted their hope and further reinforced the motivation to quit; and the desire to quit and the ability to imagine a new way of living were the most powerful motivators to quit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reasons why people with long-term SUDs stop abusing substances and the factors that influence this process.
the reasons why people stop using drugs.
the question of why people with substance use disorders stop abusing substances, and how they do so.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the factors influencing reasoning and decision making in the process of quitting substance use include harmful consequences, significant events, pressure and concern from family members, the ability to imagine a different future, and awareness of existing treatment and support options.
the study found that participants in long-term recovery had a strong motivation to quit substance use, and they were able to identify the events and people that helped them quit.
this study provides evidence that the reasons for quitting substance abuse may be more important in treatment than previously recognized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants in our study had a variety of factors that influenced their decisions to stop using.

the most significant factors that influence reasoning about quitting substance abuse are (a) the consequences of substance use, (b) the support of family and friends, (c) the ability to imagine a different future, (d) the awareness of existing options for treatment, (e) the desire to be healthy and to be able to function better, and (f) hope.
the most effective interventions for substance use disorder are the ones that help people understand why they want to change, what they want to change to, and how they can get there.
